ReSaverHelper 2: fix crash when the game is busy

A main-thread task captured the request's stack by reference. When the
game stalled longer than the 3 s wait, the request gave up, its stack was
gone, and the task wrote into it when the game finally ran it (crash in
std::string assignment after a 12 s stall). Tasks now own their data
(values and shared_ptr copies), the wait is 30 s, and a set-stage request
that times out reports 'queued' instead of failing.

Rollouts: play to the game's end once the bag is empty, instead of stopping at a leaf

The leaf network trains only on turns that began with tiles in the bag, so a
leaf reached with the bag empty is outside its training rows. With both racks
known and nothing to draw, the hasty playout is deterministic: the exact
value an endgame-trained leaf would only approximate. The kernel and the CPU
reference keep playing after their two plies while the bag is empty; two
scoreless turns in a row end such a game as six would.

Keep the screensaver away while a Steam game window is open (#36)

The stock rule only inhibits idle for fullscreen windows. Games drop out
of fullscreen during launches, intros and DLSS host restarts, and wheel
or pad input does not reset the keyboard/mouse idle timer, so NFSU2 could
hit the screensaver mid-session. Inhibit idle for every steam_app_*
window instead; "focus" would lapse whenever another monitor has focus.

fix: test the LockedHandle before dereferencing it in the game bindings (#127)

Unwrap returns a LockedHandle whose pointer is null when the receiver is
not a wrapper of the class (a method or getter lifted onto a foreign
object; V8 14 has no AccessorSignature to stop that). Every game-handle
binding went straight to `if (!*data)`, dereferencing that null pointer:
an overnight bot run crashed in Unit.getState with a read of 0x8.

Test `!data || !*data` (and `data && *data`) everywhere, so such a call
returns undefined / false like a unit that no longer exists.

intuition: RemakeDisplay() must not hold the IBase lock while calling RethinkDisplay() (#1773)

* intuition: RemakeDisplay() must not hold the IBase lock while calling RethinkDisplay()

RethinkDisplay() runs its work in the input.device task through
DoSyncAction(), and that work takes the IBase lock. RemakeDisplay() called
it with the lock still held, so any caller other than input.device itself
deadlocked: the caller waits for the input.device task, which waits for
the lock.

Release the lock after the MakeVPort() loop and before RethinkDisplay().

The import's clientGameId is "chesscom

Send moves instead of whole positions between players (#30)

Each move went over the data channel as a full FEN, and the receiver
applied it with game.load(). That reset chess.js's history every turn, so
a draw by threefold repetition could never be detected, and it accepted
any well-formed board without checking it followed the rules.

Now the mover sends just the move ("e2e4", or "e7e8q" for a promotion)
and the receiver plays it with game.move(). chess.js keeps its history
and rejects illegal moves; a malformed, out-of-turn or illegal move shows
the error card.

bc2cpp: element-returning sends carry the guarded element hint

ELEMENT_CLASS_SUPPORT treated every core call as UNKNOWN, so a value
from `a.first`, `a.last` or `a.find { }` lost the element class of an
Array whose elements were known. Those sends (and detect, min_by,
max_by), with no arguments, now answer the receiver's element hint
(ELEMENT_PICK_SENDS). The fact stays a guarded hint: consumers re-check
the class. Game::Actors#all is declared -> Array[Game::Actor]: every
value of @all is an Actor.new.

BC2CPP_ELEMENT_PICKS=0 turns it off; checked by
scripts/bc2cpp/element_picks_check.rb.

Android: two threads spun a core each at 100 % (SDK patch)

- PosixConditionBase::WaitMultiple cast the time left to whole
  milliseconds: under 1 ms it slept 0 ms, and the alertable waits (1 ms
  slices) turned every multi-object wait into a busy loop. Sleeps keep
  the clock's precision now.
- SDL on Android: each pump adds a POLL_SENTINEL, which wakes
  SDL_WaitEvent at once, so the UI thread never slept. The sentinel is
  turned off on Android (only SDL_PollEvent loops use it); controllers
  are still pumped on each game read.

Emulator, title screen: the whole game went from 4-5 busy core

cps3: SH2 DMA reads BIOS and program flash undecrypted, as in MAME

On the hardware the SH2 DMA bypasses the decryption. MAME emulates it
by reapplying the encryption to the data the DMA reads from the BIOS and
the program flash (not on sfiii2), which is what made the per game, per
pc ROM test hacks unnecessary. Do the same through a new
Sh2SetDmaReadCallback(), and decrypt the whole BIOS instead of leaving
the flash commands it transfers by DMA encrypted.
